extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent applicants/attorneys (practitioners appearing before the PTAB)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules and criteria governing ex parte appeals to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB), including who may appeal, timing, fees, what must be in an appeal brief, docketing, record/evidence rules, interviews, pre-appeal review, reinstatement, and remand. Directed at examiners and practitioners handling appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of Board / three-member panels
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 6: The Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB) consists of the Director, Deputy Director, Commissioners, and administrative patent judges; appeals, derivation proceedings, post-grant and inter partes reviews shall be heard by at least three members of the Board, designated by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative patent judges must be persons of competent legal knowledge and scientific ability. Only the PTAB may grant rehearings. Treat any reference to BPAI or predecessor organizations as reference to PTAB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe line between Board jurisdiction and Director petition
rubrics_metrics.description: The line of demarcation between appealable matters for the Board and petitionable matters for the Director should be carefully observed; the Board will not ordinarily hear a question that should be decided by the Director on petition, and the Director will not ordinarily entertain a petition where the question is appealable to the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because certain petitions have strict time windows (e.g., 2 months under 37 CFR 1.181(f)), petitionable matters will rarely be present once a case is before the Board. Examiners and applicants should choose the appropriate route (petition vs appeal) and be mindful of timing rules and remedies (see example In re Watkinson).

rubrics_metrics.name: Docketing procedure and Board notification
rubrics_metrics.description: When an appealed application is ready for docketing the Board will (A) assign an appeal number, (B) issue a docketing notice, and (C) assign the appeal to a master docket or directly to a panel of at least three Board members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board aims to notify the appellant within one month of receipt that the appeal has been received and docketed, or that the appeal is being remanded to the examiner for unresolved matters. If appeal cannot be docketed, the appeal will be remanded with an order indicating why and a copy mailed to the appellant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special-case status continues through appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: An application made special and advanced out of turn will continue to be special through its entire course of prosecution in the Office, including any appeal to the Board, subject to diligent prosecution by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition to make special after an appeal has been forwarded may be addressed to the Board, but will not be granted unless the brief has been filed and applicant meets the showing required by the Director under 37 CFR 1.102; diligent prosecution is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file a notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 134 and 37 CFR 41.31: An applicant any of whose claims has been twice rejected may appeal to the Board by filing a notice of appeal accompanied by the fee; a patent owner in certain reexamination proceedings may also appeal under specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'twice rejected' requirement need not be within the same application (e.g., rejections in parent and continuing applications count). Specific rules apply for ex parte reexamination depending on filing date. Time for filing and applicable fees are governed by 37 CFR and 35 U.S.C. 41.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of appeal must be filed within the period for reply set in the last Office action (normally 3 months for applications); may be filed up to 6 months with an appropriate petition and fee under 37 CFR 1.136(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If notice is not timely, the appeal may be dismissed. Time periods can be extendable under appropriate CFR provisions (e.g., 1.136).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal presumed from rejection of all claims under rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 41.31(c), an appeal, when taken, is presumed to be taken from the rejection of all claims under rejection unless cancelled by an amendment entered by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant does not cancel claims they do not wish to appeal and also fails to provide any argument directed to those claims in the appeal brief, any challenge to that rejection is waived and the Board may affirm rejections against such claims (see Hyatt v. Dudas).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements for notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The signature requirements of §§ 1.33 and 11.18(a) do not apply to a notice of appeal filed under 37 CFR 41.31; notices may be unsigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elimination of signature requirement for the notice of appeal does not affect signature requirements for other papers or for actions contained within the notice (e.g., authorizations to charge fees). An unsigned notice that contains an unsigned authorization to charge a deposit account will be unacceptable because the fee is lacking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for appeal (notice, brief, oral hearing, forwarding)
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 41(a)(6) and 37 CFR 41.20: Fees include a fee for filing a notice of appeal, a fee for filing an appeal brief, and a fee for requesting an oral hearing; effective March 19, 2013 the fee for filing an appeal brief was reduced to $0 and a forwarding fee for forwarding an appeal after the examiner's answer was added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay attention to current 37 CFR 41.20 rates and the forwarding fee (37 CFR 41.20(b)(4)). Even where appeal brief fee is $0, other forwarding/payment timing rules (e.g., 41.45) apply to avoid dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defective notice of appeal procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices of appeal are reviewed by the Patent Appeal Center; if defective the Office will notify the applicant of the non-compliance. A notice is defective if it was not timely filed or the notice of appeal fee was not timely filed, or if none of the applicant's claims had been twice rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications indicating defects should be sent by the Patent Appeal Center (e.g., PTOL-461). If defects are identified after the notice is entered, examiner should contact the Patent Appeal Center to determine appropriate action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal brief filing treated as notice of appeal if no notice filed
rubrics_metrics.description: When appellant files an appeal brief without first filing a notice of appeal, the Office treats the appeal brief as a notice of appeal and an appeal brief; the brief must be filed within the reply period in the last Office action and be accompanied by the appropriate fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective March 19, 2013, because the fee for filing an appeal brief is $0, appeal briefs will not be held defective for failure to pay that fee or make any statement about it for as long as the fee remains $0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on filing appeal while prosecution is pending (RCE/reply under 1.111)
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of appeal is premature if filed after applicant filed a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 to a second non-final rejection and before the Office considers that reply; applicant must wait until the examiner considers the reply and issues an action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing an appeal while the Office has not yet decided an earlier-filed reply results in the notice being defective and the Office will process the reply under 1.111 in due course. Similarly, filing an appeal with an RCE present is not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments filed with/after appeal and 37 CFR 1.116
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment filed after a final action with a notice of appeal may not be entered as a matter of right under 37 CFR 1.116; such an amendment may be admitted if it cancels claims or complies with explicit form requirements, or presents rejected claims in better form for consideration on appeal, or amends the specification upon a showing of good and sufficient reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appellant files an amendment, notice of appeal and appeal brief on the same date after mailing of a final action, 37 CFR 1.116 applies; examiners should apply requirements for entry of such amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of appeal after prosecution reopened
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant wishes to reinstate an appeal after prosecution is reopened, appellant must file a new notice of appeal in compliance with 37 CFR 41.31 and a complete new appeal brief in compliance with 37 CFR 41.37.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previously paid appeal fees will be applied to the new appeal on the same application as long as a final Board decision has not been made on the prior appeal. If fees increased, appellant must pay the difference. A complete new appeal brief is due within two months of filing the new notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Appeal Brief Review (pilot) process
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a properly filed request for pre-appeal brief review, a supervisor will designate a panel of appropriate examiners (including at least a supervisor and the examiner of record) to review appellant's remarks and the examiner's rejections; reviewers have authority to reopen prosecution if appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presenting a pre-appeal review request does not change the fee to file a notice of appeal and does not require a separate fee. Appellant may not attend the review and no interviews will be granted prior to issuance of the decision. Submission may extend the period to file an appeal brief until decision on the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews after notice of appeal rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally one interview after final rejection is permitted before an appeal brief is filed; no interviews are permitted after the appeal brief is filed except in unusual circumstances. Interviews after mailing of an examiner's answer and prior to payment of forwarding fee are generally not permitted and may confuse the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for interviews on cases under Board jurisdiction require specific approval of the Technology Center Director upon a written showing of extraordinary circumstances justifying a remand. Unusual situations (e.g., appellant wishes to cancel all appealed claims) may permit interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Record on Appeal — definition and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: The official 'Record' on appeal contains the items listed in the content listing of the Image File Wrapper (or official file) excluding amendments, Evidence, and other documents that were not entered; IDS or petitions held in abeyance while Board has jurisdiction are excluded until entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excluding non-entered documents reflects that the Board's review is properly based on the record of all entered documents. Physical items not scanned are referenced in the Image File Wrapper's content listing (artifact files, original drawings, sequence listings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Evidence' and exclusion of dictionaries
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 41.30 defines 'Evidence' to include testimony, documents and tangible objects that tend to prove or disprove a fact; for the purposes of this subpart, 'Evidence' does not include dictionaries, which may be cited before the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excluding dictionaries from 'Evidence' allows appellants and examiners to cite dictionaries in briefs and answers without triggering new-ground rules (37 CFR 41.33(d)(2) or 41.39(a)(2)). This is consistent with case law allowing courts to consult dictionaries as aids to understanding (e.g., Phillips v. AWH).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal brief timing and dismissal for failure to file
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 41.37(a)-(b): Appellant must file an appeal brief within two months from the date of filing the notice of appeal; failure to file the brief within that period causes the appeal to stand dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appeal brief fee may be $0, but other fees (e.g., forwarding fee) and timing obligations (per 41.45) remain. Extensions and petitions for additional time must follow applicable CFR rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal brief content — required headings and order
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 41.37(c): The brief shall contain specified items under appropriate headings and in the order indicated (except certain items may be relaxed for unrepresented appellants), including: (i) Real party in interest; (ii) Related appeals/interferences/trials; (iii) Summary of claimed subject matter (concise explanation with specification references); (iv) Arguments for each rejection; and additional required sections per the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each rejected independent claim and for dependent claims argued separately, if the claim contains a means-plus-function (35 U.S.C. 112(f)) recitation, the concise explanation must identify the corresponding structure, material, or acts described in the specification. Unrepresented appellants need only substantially comply with certain subsections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and method recommendations for filing notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a separate letter containing the notice of appeal is strongly recommended; Form PTO/SB/31 or Form PTO/AIA/31 may be used for filing a notice of appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a separate notice letter helps clarity and avoids treating other papers as the notice. If a brief is filed without a separate notice, the Office treats it as both notice and brief (see earlier metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of rules to reexamination and inter partes reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: This chapter is primarily directed to ex parte appeals; appeals in inter partes reexamination proceedings are governed by 37 CFR 41.60 to 41.81 and MPEP § 2674–§ 2683; 37 CFR 41.30–41.54 do not apply to inter partes reexamination appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners and practitioners must consult the correct CFR sections and MPEP chapters for reexamination-specific appeal rules (timing and eligibility differ depending on filing dates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Appeal Center review and examiner responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board's responsibility for determining whether an appeal brief is compliant is a transfer of responsibility to notify appellant of non-compliance; the Patent Examining Corps retains jurisdiction to consider appeal briefs, conduct appeal conferences, draft examiner's answers, and decide entry of amendments/evidence filed after final or after notice of appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should not preemptively mark notices/briefs defective; if a substantial defect is identified after reviews, contact the Patent Appeal Center. The Patent Appeal Center may return the application to the examiner for corrections to examiner's answer or outgoing documents when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver by failure to argue claims in brief
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant fails to provide any argument in the appeal brief directed to certain claims (which were not cancelled), any challenge to that ground of rejection has been waived and the Board may affirm rejections as to those claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellants should cancel claims they do not wish to pursue or provide argument in the brief; examiners and practitioners should note waiver consequences (see Hyatt v. Dudas).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension and payment rules when fees have changed
rubrics_metrics.description: If appeal fees were previously paid and appellant reinstates an appeal after reopening, previously paid fees will be applied to a new appeal if no final Board decision was made; if fees increased since payment, appellant must pay the difference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor fee schedules and ensure timely payment of any additional amounts required when re-filing or reinstating appeals. Deadlines for filing new briefs (e.g., two months) still apply.
